question: Should OpenClaw accept `includeFamily` as the public Gateway/tool/model-facing contract for opt-in reset-family transcript history, with `includeFamily` plus `offset` rejected?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but exposing archived reset-family transcript content through a model-facing tool is an API and security-boundary decision that automation should not make unilaterally.

options.title: Accept bounded includeFamily
options.body: Land after final exact-head review/CI with `includeFamily` as the explicit opt-in family-history selector and no offset pagination for family reads.

options.title: Reshape API before merge
options.body: Ask the author to rename or restructure the selector, response metadata, or pagination semantics before accepting the public contract.

options.title: Pause for archive design
options.body: Close or pause this PR in favor of a broader archive/export/history design if maintainers do not want a model-facing family-history selector.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded includeFamily
recommendation.body: Land after final exact-head review/CI with `includeFamily` as the explicit opt-in family-history selector and no offset pagination for family reads.
